judged_text: The prisma.app.findUnique queries only to select the slug that was just read from the request body, which is then used to index appStoreMetadata — `appStoreMetadata[reqBody.appSlug]` alone is equivalent. Every webhook delivery pays a pointless DB round-trip and carries a dead branch plus an `as keyof typeof` cast; deleting the query, the `if (!app)` check and the cast removes ten lines with no behavior change since the App table is seeded from the same metadata source.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), it does `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug }, select: { slug: true } })` and then immediately uses only that `slug` to index `appStoreMetadata` (`appStoreMetadata[app.slug as ...]`). From the diff alone, this DB lookup does not contribute any additional data beyond existence checking, and the subsequent `appMetadata` lookup already validates the slug. So the finding about an avoidable per-request DB round-trip and unnecessary cast is concretely grounded, though the claim of "no behavior change" depends on assumptions about DB seeding that are not shown in the diff.
